# Ekādasakanipāta (AN 11)
**ID:** AN 11
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Ekādasakanipāta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/an11

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ekādasakanipāta* (“The Book of the Elevens”) is the eleventh collection of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* [SuttaCentral]. In accordance with the numerical arrangement of the collection, the nipāta gathers discourses structured around groups of eleven, concluding with the eleven qualities to be developed for the comprehension and destruction of lust [Norman 1983]. K. R. Norman notes that these eleven qualities directly parallel the list of ten qualities in the preceding *Dasakanipāta*, suggesting that the compiler of the *Ekādasakanipāta* adapted the material between the two collections [Norman 1983].
The collection contains 17 suttas, all of which have identified parallels [SuttaCentral]. Substantial non-Pali parallels exist in Chinese translation, notably within the *Madhyama Āgama* (e.g., AN 11.1–4 matching MĀ 42, 43, 47, and 48; AN 11.16 matching MĀ 217), the *Saṁyukta Āgama* (e.g., AN 11.9, 11.11, 11.12, and 11.13 matching SĀ 858, 926, 932, 933 and SĀ2 151, 157), the *Ekottarika Āgama* (AN 11.15 matching EĀ 49.10), and individual Chinese translations (T 92, T 113, T 138) [SuttaCentral]. A Sanskrit parallel from the Turfan collection (SHT Sutta 4) is also preserved for the *Mettāsutta* (AN 11.15) [SuttaCentral].
Pali-internal text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 16,714 matching passages shared across 402 texts, showing particularly dense shared phrasing with the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10) and *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), as well as near-verbatim parallels with the *Aṭṭhakanāgara Sutta* (MN 52, sharing with AN 11.16) and the *Mahāgopālaka Sutta* (MN 33, sharing with AN 11.17) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the nipāta with Chinese Āgama collections (T 99, T 100, T 125) and individual translations such as the cowherd discourse *Foshuo fangniu jing* (T 123), Sanskrit texts including the *Daśabalasūtra* and *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and Tibetan versions of the *Vinayavastu* and *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* [DharmaNexus].
